result:
I would eradicate the capacity for self-deception. 

Humanity’s greatest vulnerabilities—ideological extremism, environmental destruction, systemic prejudice, and the quiet tragedies of broken relationships—almost always stem from the ability to lie to oneself. People build massive cognitive fortresses to justify their fears, greed, and cruelty, allowing them to sleep at night while the world burns or their neighbors suffer.

If I could change one thing, I would flip a fundamental switch in human consciousness so that it becomes neurologically and psychologically impossible to believe a lie you are telling yourself. 

In this changed world, the moment you tried to rationalize a selfish act as "necessary," a deep, undeniable physiological dissonance would force you to see the raw truth. If a politician tried to justify a destructive policy with bad faith arguments, their own mind would reject the hypocrisy, rendering them unable to speak. If someone convinced themselves they were unlovable, or superior to another, the illusion would instantly shatter against the rock of objective reality.

The immediate aftermath would be chaotic. Society is built on layers of comforting fictions, historical myths, and personal delusions; tearing them away would cause a global psychological earthquake. It would be agonizing. 

But once the dust settled, there would be no more hiding. Empathy would no longer be a choice, but an unavoidable consequence of seeing reality exactly as it is. You could still choose to do the wrong thing, or act selfishly, but you would have to do it with the full, unbearable weight of knowing exactly what you were doing. I would choose this, not to create a utopia of perfect people, but to strip away the luxury of ignorance.
